reviews.title: Well worth it. Versatile mouse for everything.
reviews.comment:
I’m 6’3 if that is relevant.
So I absolutely love this mouse. I’ve used several from razer to Logitech, to redragon, and other Corsair.  But this one is it. It’s super customizable, all the wireless modes are flawless, insane battery life, ergonmic. All buttons works so well and placed well, and clearly high quality. I was excited for this to come out and bought at full price when it did.
Connectivity is great too on all the modes.
And the weight makes it easy to control.
10/10 I know I’ll be using this for years!
I use this all day for work, and all leisure for gaming.

reviews.title: Great for Large Hands, But Software Dependence Is Annoying
reviews.comment:
4 stars. Finding a mouse that actually fits large hands comfortably is harder than it should be, but the Corsair Ironclaw does a really good job. For reference, I wear XXL gloves and this mouse feels much more natural than a lot of smaller gaming mice that force your hand into a cramped grip. The ergonomic shape is definitely the standout feature for me.
The build quality also seems solid so far. The buttons feel responsive, tracking is smooth, and overall it feels like a premium product. Battery life and wireless performance have both been good in my experience as well.
The biggest downside is the software dependency. You pretty much need the Corsair iCUE app to fully control and customize all the functions, which becomes an issue if you want to use it on a locked-down work computer where you can’t install software. That limits some of the mouse’s potential outside of personal gaming setups.
Price is another factor. It’s definitely on the expensive side for a mouse, but at least the quality and comfort mostly justify the cost. Overall, it’s a very good option if you have larger hands and want something comfortable for long sessions.
